title: Indraprastha Medical (INDRAMEDCO) - LIVE deep dive #4, first healthcare draw (protocol v1.4 stages 2-7): method test, no verdict; card v1.3 size 0; 7 live calls
body: LIVE method test (L9, L21): random draw (Random(20261201)) from 102 pharma/healthcare + IT-services names (44 NSE-index-classified + 58 hand-classified before the shuffle) in the India Rs 1,000-20,000 cr band; no buy/sell verdict. Research, not advice. SKIPS: EXPLEOSOL (PEAD Q2 FY27 SUE -0.32 -> quintile 2, event 14-Nov-2026, inside the avoid window), 63MOONS (governance: NSEL payment-default legacy and ongoing NSEL creditor scheme/litigation naming the group; also PEAD quintile 2 in window). SUBJECT: INDRAMEDCO (Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals, one ~700-bed hospital at Sarita Vihar, Delhi; GNCTD 26% + Apollo 22.45% = promoters 51%). Passed S2: pledge 0, unmodified audit FY26 (KAM: free-treatment litigation), no debt, solvency 0 flags, PEAD Q2 FY27 SUE +1.27 -> Q5. KEY FINDING (the whole case): the hospital land is leased from the Delhi government at Re 1/month (rent Rs 12/yr) in return for free treatment (lease: 33% IPD / 40% OPD per GNCTD); the lease EXPIRED 31-Jul-2023 and the JV agreement 10-Mar-2018 (per GNCTD affidavits reported in the press); GNCTD told the SC on 27-Jan-2026 that renewal is 'contrary to public interest'; the SC (25-Mar-2025) warned it could hand the hospital to AIIMS; GNCTD says EWS delivery was 7-10% vs the lease terms. The FY26 AR and the Q2 FY27 results notes do not mention the expiry or the affidavit (board 'noted' it on 03-Feb-2026), while the AR says the company 'remained compliant with the lease'. GNCTD did not vote its 26% at the Sep-2026 AGM and has not nominated its 3 directors incl. the Chairman; the MD's term ended 04-Nov-2026 with no successor announced. VALUATION: Rs 355.85, 17.0x trailing, 9.8x EV/EBITDA net of Rs 521 cr cash vs hospital peers 33-59x (median 48x): the discount is the lease risk; ROIC ~50% is partly the land subsidy. Price-implied P(workable renewal) ~50% [EST]. Worksheet v1.3 (legal-outcome scenarios): EV 1.35x raw / 1.39x anchored (w=0.3, raw tails ABOVE class) vs hurdle 1.76x -> card v1.3 size 0. Unit check: 63,236 discharges x 3.23 ALOS x Rs 69,714/bed-day = Rs 1,424 cr = sale of services (~560 occupied beds). Calls: 7 live (Q3 revenue, FY27 OPM, FY27 PAT, lease renewal disclosed, handover/non-renewal, MD by Mar-27, beats Nifty 500) + 3 card calls.

title: Indraprastha Medical (INDRAMEDCO) variant view, Nov 2026: cheap because the hospital's land lease has expired and the Delhi government opposes renewal; no claimable mispricing
body: Market prices a ~50% chance [EST] that IMCL keeps its hospital on workable terms (17x P/E vs peers ~48x; net cash 16% of mcap). Our view: no edge on the SC/GNCTD outcome; the evidence we found leans negative versus the company's own presentation (expiry and affidavit absent from AR FY26 and results notes; GNCTD abstained at the AGM and left its board seats empty; MD term ended without a successor; ROIC flattered by Re 1 land). Positive: net cash Rs 57/share, no debt, ARPP-led growth. Proves us wrong: a disclosed 30-year renewal near IMCL's own ask (10% IPD / 25% OPD incl. medicines) without a retrospective claim. title: Decision card INDRAMEDCO 2026-11-24 (paper)
body: Decision card v1 for Indraprastha Medical Corporation Ltd (Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals, Sarita Vihar). Rule output: size 0: blocked by Expected value vs hurdle (EV 1.39x anchored (raw 1.35x) vs hurdle 1.76x → below hurdle → size 0). Thesis: Method-test thesis: Indraprastha Medical (one ~700-bed Apollo-run hospital in Delhi) earns a ~50% ROIC partly because its land is leased from the Delhi government at Re 1/month in exchange for a free-treatment obligation it has under-delivered (7-10% vs 33% IPD / 40% OPD per GNCTD). The lease expired 31-Jul-2023 and the JV agreement 10-Mar-2018; GNCTD told the Supreme Court on 27-Jan-2026 that renewal would be 'contrary to public interest'. The 5-year outcome is a legal/political binary layered on a good operating business, not an operating-earnings call. Variant view: Market: at Rs 356 the stock trades at 17.0x trailing P/E and 9.8x EV/EBITDA net of Rs 521 cr cash, against hospital peers at 33-59x (median 48x) - a ~65% discount that IS the lease risk. A simple two-state read (going concern at ~30x = ~Rs 630/share vs handover value ~Rs 60-90/share) puts the price-implied probability of a workable renewal at roughly 50% [EST]. Our view: no claimable mispricing - we have no edge on a Supreme Court / Delhi-government outcome, and the evidence we found leans NEGATIVE relative to how the company presents it: (1) the FY26 annual report, the Q2 FY27 results notes and the MD&A do not mention that the lease and JV agreement have expired or the January affidavit (only a 3-Feb-2026 board-outcome paragraph 'noted' it), while the contingent-liability note says the company 'has remained compliant with the applicable requirements under the lease'; (2) the Delhi government (26% holder, a promoter) did not vote its shares at the 24-Sep-2026 AGM (promoter votes polled 21.44m of 46.75m) and has not nominated its 3 directors including the Chairman; (3) the MD's term ended 4-Nov-2026 with no successor announced; (4) ROIC is flattered by the land subsidy, so any renewal on market or stricter-EWS terms compresses margins. Positive offsets: Rs 521 cr net cash (16% of market cap, Rs 57/share), no debt, steady ARPP-led growth (+11% TTM revenue, 18% OPM), and courts and governments usually prefer stricter terms to closing a 700-bed hospital. What would prove us wrong: a 30-year renewal on terms close to IMCL's own ask (10% IPD / 25% OPD incl. medicines) with no retrospective claim. Departure from the outside view: our raw P(blow-up) 20% and P(<=0.5x) 26% are ABOVE the class base rates (15% / 11%) because of a specific, dated legal threat; anchored at w=0.3 (evidence note). Checked by paper calls thesis:paper-call:INDRAMEDCO:*. Open soft flags: 6. P(≥3x) 7% vs base 21%; P(≤0.5x) 26% vs base 11.3%; EV 5-yr multiple 1.35x vs hurdle 1.76x. Review 2027-02-15.

title: Delhi government affidavit opposes renewal of Indraprastha Apollo's land lease and JV agreement (27-Jan-2026)
body: In SLP(C) 29482/2009 (free-treatment matter), GNCTD told the Supreme Court that the lease of the Sarita Vihar land expired 31-Jul-2023 and the JV agreement with Apollo on 10-Mar-2018; IMCL proposed a 30-year renewal on 09-May-2025; GNCTD's 27-Jan-2026 affidavit says renewal now would be 'contrary to public interest and contractual discipline' (press reports). IMCL's board 'noted' the affidavit on 03-Feb-2026 (NSE filing 09-Feb-2026) without describing it. Earlier: SC 25-Mar-2025 warned of an AIIMS takeover; GNCTD (Nov-2025) said EWS delivery was 9-10% OPD / 7-9% IPD vs the lease's 40%/33%.

title: High ROIC built on a government-granted input (land at Re 1, a licence, a concession) is a renewal bet: find the expiry date and the counterparty's stance before trusting the return
body: Technique (INDRAMEDCO, live deep dive #4, Nov 2026): IMCL's ~50% ROIC rests on Delhi-government land at Re 1/month in exchange for a free-treatment duty. The lease expired in 2023 and the government's affidavit opposes renewal; the annual report never states the expiry. Rule: when ROIC is far above peers, list every government-granted input (land, mining lease, spectrum, concession, PPP agreement), its expiry date, the reciprocal obligation and its delivery record, and the counterparty's latest filing; read court and government filings, not the company's contingent-liability note. Treat the stock as an option on renewal terms, with tails above the class base rate.

title: A promoter that stops voting its shares (and leaves its board seats empty) is a dated governance signal: read the Reg-44 promoter 'votes polled' line
body: INDRAMEDCO, 24-Sep-2026 AGM: promoter and promoter group held 46,753,000 shares but polled 21,442,500 (45.9%) - the Delhi government's 26% stake did not vote on any resolution, and the AR says GNCTD had not nominated its 3 directors including the Chairman, while it was opposing the lease renewal in court. Cheap check: in every deep dive, compare promoter shares held vs votes polled on each AGM/postal-ballot resolution; a co-promoter abstaining signals a broken JV before any filing says so.
